results.name: mixed_parity_even_target_bias
results.description: In sets whose examples include both odd and even numbers, yes-rate for even non-example targets minus odd non-example targets; observed above the null means people favour even targets beyond what the model's (parity-symmetric given mixed examples) rules and intervals predict, below means the model over-produces an even bias.
results.code:
# name: mixed_parity_even_target_bias
# description: In sets whose examples include both odd and even numbers, yes-rate for even non-example targets minus odd non-example targets; observed above the null means people favour even targets beyond what the model's (parity-symmetric given mixed examples) rules and intervals predict, below means the model over-produces an even bias.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    fd = np.mod(E, 10)
    share_fd = np.any(fd == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    par = np.where(np.isnan(E), np.nan, np.mod(E, 2))
    mixed = (np.nanmax(par, axis=1) == 1) & (np.nanmin(par, axis=1) == 0)
    m = (~is_ex) & mixed
    return rate(m & (np.mod(t, 2) == 0)) - rate(m & (np.mod(t, 2) == 1))

results.name: single_example_distance_gradient
results.description: For single-example sets, yes-rate for non-example targets within 5 of the example minus targets more than 20 from it; observed above the null means people generalize from one example with a steeper magnitude-similarity gradient than the model's interval posterior, below means the model's gradient is too steep.

    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    fd = np.mod(E, 10)
    share_fd = np.any(fd == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)

results.name: wide_span_interior_gap_endorsement
results.description: In 3-4 example sets spanning at least 60, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the span, more than 8 from every example and sharing no final digit with any example; observed above the null means people fill the interior of widely spread sets more (diffuse range responding) than the model, below means the model's wide intervals over-fill it.
results.code:
# name: wide_span_interior_gap_endorsement
# description: In 3-4 example sets spanning at least 60, yes-rate for non-example targets strictly inside the span, more than 8 from every example and sharing no final digit with any example; observed above the null means people fill the interior of widely spread sets more (diffuse range responding) than the model, below means the model's wide intervals over-fill it.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    fd = np.mod(E, 10)
    share_fd = np.any(fd == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    lo = np.nanmin(E, axis=1)

    m = (~is_ex) & (n >= 3) & (hi - lo >= 60) & (t > lo) & (t < hi) & (dist > 8) & (~share_fd)
    return rate(m)

results.name: example_count_breadth_slope
results.description: Non-example yes-rate in 4-example sets minus in 2-example sets; observed above the null means people narrow their generalization with more examples less than the model's tempered size principle implies (below means they narrow more).

results.name: cross_position_digit_overlap
results.description: In 2-4 example sets, among non-example targets more than 10 from every example and sharing no final digit with any example, yes-rate for targets whose final digit equals some example tens digit or whose tens digit equals some example final digit, minus the rest; observed above the null means people use loose cross-position digit matching that the model's whole-set digit rules cannot produce.
results.code:
# name: cross_position_digit_overlap
# description: In 2-4 example sets, among non-example targets more than 10 from every example and sharing no final digit with any example, yes-rate for targets whose final digit equals some example tens digit or whose tens digit equals some example final digit, minus the rest; observed above the null means people use loose cross-position digit matching that the model's whole-set digit rules cannot produce.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    fd = np.mod(E, 10)
    share_fd = np.any(fd == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    tens = np.floor(E / 10)
    cross = np.any((tens == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None]) | (fd == np.floor(t / 10)[:, None]), axis=1)
    m = (~is_ex) & (~share_fd) & (dist > 10) & (n >= 2)
    return rate(m & cross) - rate(m & ~cross)

results.name: multiple_of_example_targets
results.description: In 1-2 example sets, among non-example targets more than 5 from every example and sharing no final digit with any example, yes-rate for targets that are a larger multiple of some example minus other targets; observed above the null means people generalize by "multiples of the example" more than the model's fixed rule list (multiples of 3-12 only) allows.
results.code:
# name: multiple_of_example_targets
# description: In 1-2 example sets, among non-example targets more than 5 from every example and sharing no final digit with any example, yes-rate for targets that are a larger multiple of some example minus other targets; observed above the null means people generalize by "multiples of the example" more than the model's fixed rule list (multiples of 3-12 only) allows.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    fd = np.mod(E, 10)
    share_fd = np.any(fd == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    mul = np.any((np.mod(t[:, None], E) == 0) & (t[:, None] > E), axis=1)
    m = (~is_ex) & (n <= 2) & (dist > 5) & (~share_fd)
    return rate(m & mul) - rate(m & ~mul)

results.name: pure_digit_set_neighbour_leak
results.description: In 2-4 example sets whose examples all share one final digit, yes-rate for non-example targets within 2 of an example that do not share that final digit; observed above the null means people leak magnitude similarity around a clean digit-rule set more than the model (which concentrates on the rule), below means the model leaks too much.
results.code:
# name: pure_digit_set_neighbour_leak
# description: In 2-4 example sets whose examples all share one final digit, yes-rate for non-example targets within 2 of an example that do not share that final digit; observed above the null means people leak magnitude similarity around a clean digit-rule set more than the model (which concentrates on the rule), below means the model leaks too much.
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    fd = np.mod(E, 10)
    share_fd = np.any(fd == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    fdm = np.where(np.isnan(E), np.nan, fd)
    pure = (np.nanmax(fdm, axis=1) == np.nanmin(fdm, axis=1)) & (n >= 2)
    m = (~is_ex) & pure & (dist <= 2) & (~share_fd)
    return rate(m)

results.name: round_number_target_effect
results.description: Among sets with no example that is a multiple of 10, yes-rate for non-example targets more than 10 from every example that are multiples of 10 minus other such targets; observed below the null means people avoid round-number targets more than the model predicts (above means they favour them more).
results.code:
# name: round_number_target_effect
# description: Among sets with no example that is a multiple of 10, yes-rate for non-example targets more than 10 from every example that are multiples of 10 minus other such targets; observed below the null means people avoid round-number targets more than the model predicts (above means they favour them more).
def test_statistic(df):
    E = df["number_set"].astype(str).str.split(",", expand=True).reindex(columns=range(4)).apply(pd.to_numeric, errors="coerce").to_numpy(dtype=float)
    t = df["target"].astype(float).to_numpy()
    r = df["rating"].to_numpy().astype(float)
    n = np.sum(~np.isnan(E), axis=1)
    is_ex = np.any(E == t[:, None], axis=1)
    dist = np.nanmin(np.abs(E - t[:, None]), axis=1)
    fd = np.mod(E, 10)
    share_fd = np.any(fd == np.mod(t, 10)[:, None], axis=1)
    def rate(m):
        return float(r[m].mean()) if m.sum() > 0 else 0.0
    any10 = np.any(fd == 0, axis=1)
    m = (~is_ex) & (~any10) & (dist > 10)
    return rate(m & (np.mod(t, 10) == 0)) - rate(m & (np.mod(t, 10) != 0))
